text:
maya: CI failure on sdk-node publish after typegen regen. npm publish errors out with auth + semver guard. Repro below, opening thread so we can coordinate.

maya: ```
$ ./scripts/release-sdk.sh node
> building packages...
> typegen: regenerated types for openapi v1.42.0 -> changed exports order
> npm publish --access public packages/sdk-node
npm ERR! code E401
npm ERR! 401 Unauthorized - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@redwood-inference/sdk-node - You must authenticate to publish packages.
Publishing aborted due to semver guard: detected source changes but no changelog fragment for minor bump.
```

devex-bot: CI job #4512 failed: workflow=publish-sdk, step=publish-npm, status=failed, reason="auth/semver-guard" :robot_face:

james: copying logs, thx. quick q — did the typegen actually increment version in package.json or just reorder files?

maya: it didn't touch package.json version, but our publish flow runs a diff between last published dist and current dist. The reorder triggers the semver-diff detector and it expects a changelog fragment for any minor/major-level change.

ryan: ah our semver/changelog validator rejects publishes with non-trivial API diffs unless changelog fragment exists. link: https://ci.internal/reports/semver-guard (CI job shows the exact diff)

sara: we've hit this pattern when OpenAPI adds optional fields -> typegen output changes shape. Quick mitigation is to add a changelog fragment explaining the non-breaking export reorder and rerun.

lee: also noticing the npm auth failures — the runner tried 3 immediate retries and wiped the token via an env rotation. The auth/retry lib in publish step uses fixed-interval retries, which means the registry throttled us. Need exponential backoff + token refresh.

james: so two separate issues: (A) semver/changelog guard tripped by harmless typegen reorder; (B) auth flakiness during publish. Which one to tackle first? Auth is blocking the re-run, so probably that.

maya: workaround: I can requeue with a fresh token in CI for now, but we should patch the retry behavior. I'll re-run after adding a tiny changelog fragment to satisfy guard.

devex-bot: Job #4513 queued by maya.

ryan: can we also add a lightweight test in the sampleapp onboarding pipeline to catch publish-time 401 -> retry cascade? If sample apps fail on onboarding because of auth/retry, new users hit friction fast. I opened PR: https://git.internal/pr/5678 (adds e2e that simulates token expiry and ensures exponential backoff)

sara: :thumbsup: after publish succeeds, let's update the dev onboarding doc (docs/dev/onboarding.md) to note the typegen->changelog footgun and how to add fragments: `scripts/changelog/fragments/new-sdk-node.md`

james: for medium-term: we should relax the semver-diff detector to ignore purely reordering-only diffs or add a typegen-aware post-processor that normalizes exports before diffing. That would avoid noisy bumps. Filing an RFC ticket.

lee: I'll open the patch PR for auth retry now, small change in publish action to use our retry util with backoff. assign to james for review. ETA ~2h.

maya: plan: (1) add changelog fragment + re-run job #4513 (done by me), (2) lee opens hotfix PR for retry (in review), (3) james & ryan add followups: semver-diff normalization + sampleapp e2e. I'll report back on success/failure in this thread.

lee: PR created: https://git.internal/pr/5680 — patch uses exponential backoff, max 5 retries, adds token-refresh hook.

maya: re-run succeeded! Job #4513 -> publish succeeded, npm package published as @redwood-inference/sdk-node@0.12.1. Will run sampleapp smoke now.

sara: amazing — thanks. once smoke passes, we should cherry-pick the changelog fragment to the release notes so release automation picks it up for the changelog generation.

ryan: smoke passed in staging. sampleapp onboarding no longer hits the 401 loop. Good to close this out and track the normalization work for typegen diffs.

maya: closing loop: job #4513 published, PR #5680 (retry) merged to main, PR for semver-diff normalization filed (RFC-213). Thanks everyone.

maya: tagging follow-ups: @james (review RFC), @ryan (sampleapp e2e), @sara (changelog docs).
